items.followUp: What is a cofactor? Name one example.

rubric.why: A coenzyme is an organic, non-protein substance that works with an enzyme.
rubric.description: Defines a coenzyme as an organic, non-protein substance associated with an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as organic and non-protein, or as an organic helper of an enzyme.

rubric.why: Coenzymes assist enzyme action, commonly by transferring chemical groups or electrons.
rubric.description: States one function of a coenzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid function such as transferring groups or electrons, or assisting enzyme action.

modelAnswer: A co-enzyme is an organic, non-protein substance that associates with an enzyme and helps it work.
It assists enzyme action by transferring chemical groups or electrons between reactions.

items.followUp: How are enzymes used in cheese-making?

rubric.why: Enzymes break down starch into sugars that yeast can use.
rubric.description: Explains that enzymes convert starch into fermentable sugars.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming starch as the starting material and sugar or fermentable sugar as the product.

rubric.why: Yeast ferments the sugars to produce alcohol in brewing.
rubric.description: Connects the sugars to alcohol production by fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that yeast ferments the sugars to make alcohol.

modelAnswer: In brewing, enzymes break down starch in grains into fermentable sugars.
Yeast ferments these sugars to produce alcohol.

items.followUp: Define optimum temperature and give an example of an enzyme that works best at a high temperature.

rubric.why: Optimum pH is the pH at which an enzyme has its greatest activity or reaction rate.
rubric.description: Defines optimum pH as the pH at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking a particular pH to maximum enzyme activity or reaction rate.

rubric.why: Pepsin works best in acidic conditions (about pH 2); trypsin works best in alkaline conditions (about pH 8).
rubric.description: Gives a valid enzyme example with its optimum pH or corresponding condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct enzyme and matching optimum pH or condition.

modelAnswer: Optimum pH is the pH at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
For example, pepsin has an optimum pH of about 2.

items.followUp: Name two essential elements commonly supplied to crops by fertilizers.

rubric.why: Fertilizers are materials added to soil.
rubric.description: Identifies fertilizers as materials or substances added to soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fertilizers are added to soil.

rubric.why: Fertilizers supply essential nutrients or elements and improve soil fertility or plant growth.
rubric.description: States that fertilizers supply essential nutrients/elements or improve fertility.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the purpose of supplying nutrients/elements or improving fertility.

modelAnswer: Fertilizers are substances added to soil to supply essential elements needed by plants.
They improve soil fertility and promote plant growth.

items.followUp: Name four foods that are good sources of protein.

rubric.why: The question asks for four protein sources; examples include meat, fish, eggs, milk, pulses, beans and lentils.
rubric.description: Names four valid sources of protein.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for any four correct sources; accept other valid food sources of protein.

modelAnswer: Four sources of protein are meat, fish, eggs and pulses.

items.followUp: What is the role of root pressure in the upward movement of water?

rubric.why: Loss of water by transpiration creates a pulling force that draws water upward through the xylem.
rubric.description: Defines transpirational pull as the force created by transpiration that draws water upward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking transpiration to an upward pull or movement of water through xylem.

rubric.why: This pull helps in the ascent of sap and the transport of water and mineral salts from roots to leaves.
rubric.description: Gives an advantage of transpirational pull.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid advantage, such as aiding ascent of sap or moving water/minerals from roots to leaves.

modelAnswer: Transpirational pull is the pulling force produced by transpiration that draws water upward through the xylem.
It helps in the ascent of sap and transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves.

items.followUp: What are basophils? State one function.

rubric.why: Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell, specifically a granular leukocyte.
rubric.description: Identifies eosinophils as a type of white blood cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as white blood cells or granular leukocytes.

rubric.why: Eosinophils help defend against parasites and are involved in allergic reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning defence against parasites or a role in allergic reactions.

modelAnswer: Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell.
They help defend the body against parasites.

items.followUp: Describe the cellular level and organ level of biological organization.

rubric.why: At the molecular level, atoms combine to form molecules, including large biological molecules.
rubric.description: Describes the molecular level as involving atoms and molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms form molecules or naming biological macromolecules.

rubric.why: Examples of molecules at this level include proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a biological molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least one correct example of a biological molecule.

rubric.why: A tissue is made of similar cells, usually of common origin, working together.
rubric.description: Defines a tissue as a group of similar cells working together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the group-of-similar-cells idea.

rubric.why: The cells in a tissue cooperate to perform a particular function.
rubric.description: States that tissue cells perform a common or specific function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the shared function of the cells.

rubric.why: Examples include xylem tissue transporting water, phloem transporting food, muscle tissue contracting, and epithelial tissue providing protection.
rubric.description: Gives a correct tissue example and its function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid tissue and associated function.

modelAnswer: At the molecular level, atoms combine to form molecules and large biological molecules such as proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids.
These molecules are the chemical components of cells and their structures.
At the tissue level, a tissue is a group of similar cells, usually of common origin, that work together.
The cells of a tissue perform a particular function.
For example, xylem tissue transports water in plants.
